rows.title: Open Norwegian bank account — D-number is a prerequisite
rows.official_guidance: Most Norwegian banks require a Norwegian D-number or national identity number to open an account.
rows.actual_reality: DNB and Nordea will open accounts for EU nationals with a D-number only. Sbanken (now DNB) used to accept passports alone but no longer does. Without a Norwegian account, the employer cannot run payroll and the employee cannot receive salary. The D-number → bank account → payroll chain is sequential and cannot be parallelised.
rows.action_required_hr: Ensure D-number is secured before the employee attempts to open a bank account. Provide a letter confirming employment and salary for the bank application.
rows.action_required_employee: Visit a bank branch in person with passport, D-number documentation, proof of address, and HR employment letter.
rows.timeline_label: D+14 after arrival: Open bank account as soon as D-number is received
rows.notes: High decay risk — bank policies on D-number requirements change frequently. Verify at each review.

rows.title: Register employee with NAV (Norwegian Labour and Welfare Administration)
rows.official_guidance: Employers must register all employees working in Norway with NAV. This triggers entitlement to sickness benefit, parental leave, and unemployment insurance under the Norwegian social security system.
rows.actual_reality: Registration must happen before the first working day, not within 30 days as many HR teams assume based on French practice. Late registration results in the employee being uninsured during the gap period, which creates employer liability.
rows.action_required_hr: Submit A-melding (payroll and employment reporting) to Altinn before the employee's first working day. Engage a Norwegian payroll bureau if not already set up.
rows.action_required_employee: Provide HR with Norwegian bank account details and D-number as soon as both are available.
rows.timeline_label: D-7: NAV registration must be in place before first working day

rows.title: Register with local police within 3 months of arrival
rows.official_guidance: EU/EEA nationals exercising their right to free movement in Norway must register with the police (UDI registration) if staying longer than 3 months.
rows.actual_reality: UDI appointment slots at Oslo police district routinely book out 6-8 weeks in advance. Employees must book within the first 2 weeks of arrival or risk being unable to register before the 3-month deadline.
rows.action_required_hr: Send employee the UDI online booking link before departure. Brief them that slots fill fast and booking must happen on or before Day 1 in Oslo.
rows.action_required_employee: Book police registration appointment online via politiet.no immediately upon arrival. Bring employment contract, passport, and proof of address.
rows.timeline_label: D+14 after arrival: Book appointment immediately — slots fill in days
rows.notes: Founder-verified. Slot scarcity is the non-obvious element — official guidance says 3 months but practical reality is book within 2 weeks.

rows.title: Apply for Norwegian D-number before first payroll run
rows.official_guidance: Employees working in Norway require a D-number (temporary identification number) issued by the Tax Administration (Skatteetaten) before they can be registered in the tax system.
rows.actual_reality: D-number applications take 1-4 weeks. Without it, the employee cannot be correctly taxed. Employers who run payroll without a D-number face a withholding obligation at the maximum rate (47%) and must re-run payroll once the D-number is issued — generating significant admin.
rows.action_required_hr: Initiate D-number application via Skatteetaten as soon as employment start date is confirmed. Do not begin payroll until D-number is received. Coordinate with payroll provider.
rows.action_required_employee: Attend in-person ID verification at a tax office if required. Bring passport and signed employment contract.
rows.timeline_label: D-60: Initiate D-number application — must be received before first payroll
rows.notes: Payroll re-run risk is the non-obvious flag. Many HR teams assume this can wait until arrival.

rows.title: Employer applies for Skilled Worker Permit before employee travels
rows.official_guidance: Non-EU/EEA nationals who intend to work in Norway must obtain a Skilled Worker Permit (skilled workers permit, SWP) issued by UDI before entering Norway for work purposes.
rows.actual_reality: Processing time at UDI is 8-16 weeks standard; 3-5 weeks via the fast-track scheme (available only if employer is UDI-certified). Many employers don't know about fast-track certification and lose 3 months of lead time. The employee CANNOT legally work in Norway until the permit is in hand — no work-pending-permit arrangement exists.
rows.action_required_hr: Apply for UDI employer certification if not already certified (2-4 week process). Submit Skilled Worker Permit application at minimum 16 weeks before intended start date. Monitor application status weekly via UDI portal.
rows.action_required_employee: Do not travel to Norway for work until permit is granted. Prepare supporting documents: diplomas, work experience letters, proof of qualifications relevant to the role.
rows.timeline_label: D-112: Submit SWP application — earlier if employer is not UDI-certified
rows.notes: UDI fast-track certification gap is the highest-value non-obvious item for this corridor.

rows.title: Employee collects residence card at Norwegian embassy in France
rows.official_guidance: Once the Skilled Worker Permit is granted by UDI, the employee must collect the residence card at the Norwegian embassy or consulate in the country of residence before travelling.
rows.actual_reality: The Norwegian Embassy in Paris has a 4-6 week appointment wait for permit collection. UDI issues the permit decision digitally but the physical card is only released via the embassy — the employee cannot travel without it. This step is invisible in UDI's online tracking and catches many employees off guard.
rows.action_required_hr: Alert the employee immediately when UDI issues permit approval. Provide embassy appointment booking link for Paris embassy on the same day.
rows.action_required_employee: Book Paris embassy appointment immediately upon receiving UDI permit approval. Attend in person with passport and UDI approval letter.
rows.timeline_label: D-28: Book embassy appointment immediately on UDI approval
